arxiv-1609-01397.title: Tailoring Spin Chain Dynamics for Fractional Revivals
arxiv-1609-01397.creator: Alastair Kay
arxiv-1609-01397.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Alastair Kay. The production of quantum states required for use in quantum protocols & technologies is studied by developing the tools to re-engineer a perfect state transfer spin chain so that a separable input excitation is output over multiple sites.

arxiv-2006-05014.title: HausaMT v1.0: Towards English–Hausa Neural Machine Translation
arxiv-2006-05014.creator: Adewale Akinfaderin
arxiv-2006-05014.description: Abstract Neural Machine Translation (NMT) for low-resource languages suffers from low performance because of the lack of large amounts of parallel data and language diversity. To contribute to ameliorating this problem, we built a baseline model for English–Hausa machine translation, which is considered a task for low–resource language.

arxiv-2106-03970.title: Batch Normalization Orthogonalizes Representations in Deep Random Networks Thanks: INRIA Paris, ETH Zurich, INRIA-ENS-PSL Paris.
arxiv-2106-03970.creator: Hadi Daneshmand and Amir Joudaki and Francis Bach
arxiv-2106-03970.description: Abstract . This paper underlines a subtle property of batch-normalization (BN): Successive batch normalizations with random linear transformations make hidden representations increasingly orthogonal across layers of a deep neural network. We establish a non-asymptotic characterization of the interplay between depth, width, and the orthogonality of deep representations.

arxiv-2210-07815.title: Intra-session Context-aware Feed Recommendation in Live Systems Conference: Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; October 17–21, 2022; Atlanta, GA, USA Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
arxiv-2210-07815.creator: Luo Ji, Gao Liu, Mingyang Yin, Hongxia Yang
arxiv-2210-07815.description: Abstract . Feed recommendation allows users to constantly browse items until feel uninterested and leave the session, which differs from traditional recommendation scenarios. Within a session, user’s decision to continue browsing or not substantially affects occurrences of later clicks. However, such type of exposure bias is generally ignored or not explicitly modeled in most feed recommendation studies.

arxiv-2212-01590.title: Domain-Invariant Feature Alignment Using Variational Inference For Partial Domain Adaptation
arxiv-2212-01590.creator: Sandipan Choudhuri, Suli Adeniye, Arunabha Sen, Hemanth Venkateswara
arxiv-2212-01590.description: Abstract The standard closed-set domain adaptation approaches seek to mitigate distribution discrepancies between two domains under the constraint of both sharing identical label sets. However, in realistic scenarios, finding an optimal source domain with identical label space is a challenging task.

arxiv-2305-05050.title: ANALOGICAL - A Novel Benchmark for Long Text Analogy Evaluation in Large Language Models
arxiv-2305-05050.creator: Thilini Wijesiriwardene, Ruwan Wickramarachchi, Bimal G. Gajera, Shreeyash Mukul Gowaikar, Chandan Gupta, Aman Chadha, Aishwarya Naresh Reganti, Amit Sheth, Amitava Das
arxiv-2305-05050.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Thilini Wijesiriwardene, Ruwan Wickramarachchi, Bimal G. Gajera, Shreeyash Mukul Gowaikar, Chandan Gupta, Aman Chadha, Aishwarya Naresh Reganti, Amit Sheth, Amitava Das. Over the past decade, analogies, in the form of word-level analogies, have played a significant role as an intrinsic measure of evaluating the quality of word embedding methods such as word2vec.

arxiv-2312-17170.title: Classification of multiplication modules over multiplication rings with finitely many minimal primes
arxiv-2312-17170.creator: V. V. Bavula
arxiv-2312-17170.description: Abstract A classification of multiplication modules over multiplication rings with finitely many minimal primes is obtained. A characterisation of multiplication rings with finitely many minimal primes is given via faithful, Noetherian, distributive modules. It is proven that for a multiplication ring with finitely many minimal primes every faithful, Noetherian, distributive module is a faithful multiplication module, and vice versa.

arxiv-2401-13083.title: Generalized Models for Inflationary Preheating: Oscillations and Symmetries
arxiv-2401-13083.creator: Leia Barrowes, Fred C. Adams, Anthony M. Bloch, John T. Giblin, Jr, Scott Watson
arxiv-2401-13083.description: Abstract The paradigm of the inflationary universe provides a possible explanation for several observed cosmological properties. In order for such solutions to be successful, the universe must convert the energy stored in the inflaton potential into standard model particles through a process known as reheating.

arxiv-2405-09237.title: Fast formation of large ice pebbles after FU Orionis outbursts
arxiv-2405-09237.creator: Katrin Ros & Anders Johansen
arxiv-2405-09237.description: Abstract During their formation, nascent planetary systems are subject to FU Orionis outbursts that heat a substantial part of the disc. This causes water ice in the affected part of the disc to sublimate as the ice line moves outwards to several to tens of astronomical units.

arxiv-2407-02186.title: Data-Driven Probabilistic Methodology for Aircraft Conflict Detection Under Wind Uncertainty
arxiv-2407-02186.creator: Jaime de la Mota, María Cerezo-Magaña, Alberto Olivares, Ernesto Staffetti
arxiv-2407-02186.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jaime de la Mota, María Cerezo-Magaña, Alberto Olivares, Ernesto Staffetti. Assuming the availability of a reliable aircraft trajectory planner, this paper presents a probabilistic methodology to detect conflicts between aircraft in the cruise phase of flight in the presence of wind velocity forecasting uncertainty. This uncertainty is quantified by ensemble weather forecasts, the members of which are regarded as realizations of correlated random processes and used to derive the eastward and northward components of the wind velocity.

arxiv-2409-15575.title: Quantum K K -Rings of Partial Flag Varieties, Coulomb Branches, and the Bethe Ansatz
arxiv-2409-15575.creator: Irit Huq-Kuruvilla
arxiv-2409-15575.description: Abstract . We give a purely geometric explanation of the coincidence between the Coulomb Branch equations for the 3D GLSM describing the quantum K K -theory of a flag variety, and the Bethe Ansatz equations of the 5-vertex lattice model.

arxiv-2412-18503.title: Inline-Amplification-Free Time Transfer Utilizing Waveform-Resolved Single-Photon Detection
arxiv-2412-18503.creator: Yufei Zhang, Ziyang Chen, Bin Luo, Hong Guo
arxiv-2412-18503.description: Abstract High-precision time transfer over a long haul of fiber plays a significant role in many fields. The core method, namely cascading relay nodes for the compensation of signal attenuation and dispersion, is however insufficient to deal with crucial point-to-point transfer scenarios, such as harsh environments with extremely deficient infrastructure and emergency conditions.

arxiv-2502-20788.title: Adding smoothing splines to the SAM model improves stock assessment
arxiv-2502-20788.creator: Silius M. Vandeskog 1, Magne Aldrin 1, Daniel Howell 2, Edvin Fuglebakk 2
arxiv-2502-20788.description: Abstract The stock assessment model SAM contains a large number of age-dependent parameters that must be manually grouped together to obtain robust inference. This can make the model selection process slow, non-extensive and highly subjective, while producing unrealistic looking parameter estimates with discrete jumps. We propose to model age-dependent SAM parameters using smoothing spline functions.

arxiv-2506-06407.title: TimeWak : Temporal Chained-Hashing Watermark for Time Series Data
arxiv-2506-06407.creator: Zhi Wen Soi, Chaoyi Zhu, Fouad Abiad, Aditya Shankar, Jeroen M. Galjaard, Huijuan Wang, Lydia Y. Chen
arxiv-2506-06407.description: Abstract Synthetic time series generated by diffusion models enable sharing privacy-sensitive datasets, such as patients’ functional MRI records. Key criteria for synthetic data include high data utility and traceability to verify the data source. Recent watermarking methods embed in homogeneous latent spaces, but state-of-the-art time series generators operate in real space—making latent-based watermarking incompatible.

pmc-10590048.title: Treatment of syphilitic aortitis with coronary artery bypass grafting and “open” stent placement
pmc-10590048.creator: Tiansheng Tang, Changjuan Wu, Ziao Wang, Jun Wei, Dafa Zhang, Weiyong Sheng
pmc-10590048.description: Cardiovascular syphilis manifests many years after primary infection. Here, we report the successful treatment of a patient who developed syphilitic aortitis with bilateral coronary ostial stenosis and aortic insufficiency. The patient underwent right coronary artery bypass grafting, left main coronary ostial “open” stent placement, and mechanical aortic valve placement during open-heart surgery.

pmc-11419874.title: Unlocking the in vitro and in vivo antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities of polysaccharide fractions from Lepidium sativum seed-coat mucilage
pmc-11419874.creator: Imdad Ullah Khan, Yusra Jamil, Fareeha Shams, Salman Farsi, Muhammad Humayun, Anwar Hussain, Ayaz Ahmad, Amjad Iqbal, Abdulwahed Fahad Alrefaei, Sajid Ali
pmc-11419874.description: Inflammation coupled with oxidative stress contribute to the pathogenicity of various clinical disorders. Oxidative stress arises from an imbalance between production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and antioxidant defense system, leading to cellular damages. The study investigated the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of polysaccharides isolated from Lepidium sativum seed-coat mucilage.

pmc-11663370.title: Comparing the Performance of Two Cryptococcal Antigen Detection Tests: Chemiluminescence vs Colloidal Gold Methods
pmc-11663370.creator: Xiao-yun Yu, Lei Zhang, Yueyue Hu, Zhongliang Zhu, Yongze Zhu, Xi Li
pmc-11663370.description: ObjectiveTo compare the performance of a new chemiluminescence method with that of the traditional colloidal gold method for cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) detection.MethodsCryptococcosis is a global invasive mycosis associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) testing from serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) has been regarded as the gold standard for early diagnosis.

pmc-11688588.title: Sample Size Requirements for Popular Classification Algorithms in Tabular Clinical Data: Empirical Study
pmc-11688588.creator: Scott Silvey, Jinze Liu
pmc-11688588.description: BackgroundThe performance of a classification algorithm eventually reaches a point of diminishing returns, where the additional sample added does not improve the results. Thus, there is a need to determine an optimal sample size that maximizes performance while accounting for computational burden or budgetary concerns.

pmc-12018401.title: When fiction meets reality: ethnofiction as a way of constructing youth narratives about delinquent paths
pmc-12018401.creator: Haydée Caruso
pmc-12018401.description: This article explores an ethnographic experience built with Portuguese young people in juvenile detention centers, using ethnofiction as a methodological strategy for approaching the public under investigation. The study examines the narratives that these young people constructed through a fictional character called João, whose experiences reflect the participants’ life stories and the paths that led them to commit crimes.

pmc-12649562.title: Regulation of the Expression of nucS, a Key Component of the Mismatch Repair System in Mycobacteria
pmc-12649562.creator: Esmeralda Cebrián-Sastre, Ángel Ruiz-Enamorado, Alfredo Castañeda-García, Susanne Gola, Pablo García-Bravo, Leonor Kremer, Jesús Blázquez, Anders Løbner-Olesen
pmc-12649562.description: Mismatch repair (MMR) system alterations can trigger transient hypermutation, promoting adaptive mutations under stress, such as antibiotic exposure. While most organisms use MutS and MutL protein families for MMR, many archaea and actinobacteria, including the major human pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis, lack these components and instead rely on NucS, a structurally distinct enzyme driving a non-canonical MMR pathway.

pmc-12656610.title: Incorporation of Natural Biostimulants in Biodegradable Mulch Films for Agricultural Applications: Ecotoxicological Evaluation
pmc-12656610.creator: Chelo Escrig Rondán, Celia Sevilla Gil, Pablo Sanz Fernández, Juan Francisco Ferrer Crespo, Cristina Furió Sanz
pmc-12656610.description: This study deals with the incorporation of biostimulants of natural origin in a biodegradable polymeric matrix, with the aim of developing mulch films that, when degraded in the soil, release bioactive compounds that improve soil quality and favor the agronomic growth of crops.

pmc-12733137.title: Ameliorating Acute Kidney Injury Induced by Ischemia-Reperfusion by Targeting Purine Metabolism
pmc-12733137.creator: Limei Zhao, Tingting Zhang, Xiaoshuang Zhou, Ligia Petrica
pmc-12733137.description: In the pathological process of acute kidney injury (AKI) and its transition to chronic kidney disease, the uric acid (UA) metabolic pathway plays a significant role. UA is produced as the last oxidative product in the metabolism of purine nucleotides. Prolonged organ ischemia promotes the breakdown of nucleotides into adenosine, hypoxanthine, xanthine, and UA.

pmc-12982405.title: Exploring anatomical variations of mandibular premolars and their clinical management: a case series
pmc-12982405.creator: Bridhi Jalan, Srishti Grover, Janina Loren DSouza, Annapoorna Shenoy, Nisha Gawade
pmc-12982405.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Anatomical variations in root canals pose significant challenges and may affect the course of treatment. Mandibular premolars usually have a single canal with single root. However, this case series highlights three mandibular premolars with distinct canal configurations. The first case involved a mandibular second premolar with Sert and Bayirli Type IX anatomy, characterised by one canal trifurcating into three different canals at the apex. In the second case, the Vertucci Type V configuration is in the mandibular second premolar.

pmc-13066492.title: Spontaneous speech enables scalable digital phenotyping of physical functional deficits in aging
pmc-13066492.creator: Eloïse Da Cunha, Raphaël Zory, Frédéric Chorin, Valeria Manera, Auriane Gros
pmc-13066492.description: The rising global burden of pathological aging engenders an urgent need for accessible tools enabling early detection of physical decline, which significantly impacts quality of life and healthcare systems. We hypothesized that speech analysis could capture phenotype-specific signatures of physical deterioration through shared neuromuscular pathways, offering a novel approach to physical assessment.

pmc-13148600.title: Phase and absorbance retrieval in X-ray holographic microscopy under weak illumination using physics-driven neural networks
pmc-13148600.creator: Jihwan Kim, Jun Lim, Sugeun Jo, Sungho Park, Sang Joon Lee
pmc-13148600.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A physics-driven deep learning model enables single-shot retrieval of 3D phase and absorbance from shot-noise-limited hard X-ray holograms. Validated on both synthetic and experimental data, it provides robust reconstruction under weak illumination. Introduction

X-ray holographic microscopy (XHM), originating from Gabor’s holography (Gabor, 1948 ▸), is a nondestructive three-dimensional (3D) imaging technique for visualizing internal structures of test samples (Aoki & Kikuta, 1974 ▸; Jacobsen et al., 1990 ▸; McNulty et al., 1992 ▸; Faigel & Tegze, 1999 ▸).
